builder_notes.pattern: Discriminated union vs parallel optional fields
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: When you see N url/path/media fields alongside a type discriminator field, they're a candidate for a discriminated union.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: If a type discriminator tells you which of N fields is active, fold those N fields into a union: { type: 'video'; url: string }.
builder_notes.stack_example: ItemMedia in models.ts: the switch in createItem is the proof the original was a manual discriminant.

builder_notes.pattern: validateTiersShape(_tiers) { return true } stub — function that always returns a constant
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: A doc-comment saying TypeScript enforces invariants on a function that does nothing.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: A validator that always returns true is an honesty leak. Either implement it honestly or delete it.
builder_notes.stack_example: packages/core/src/tierLogic.ts — stub deleted loop 20; no caller was affected.

builder_notes.pattern: Smart constructor doesn't close the gap unless it's the only construction path
builder_notes.how_to_recognize: Search for direct object literal construction (const x: T = { id, name }) after adding a smart constructor.
builder_notes.smallest_coding_rule: After adding a smart constructor, grep for direct construction of that type and migrate call sites one loop at a time.
